Hi Marissa,

Thanks for participating in Mosaic Bank's platform evaluation. Attached is our standard identity and admin controls questionnaire — we ask that vendors provide written answers and evidence artifacts for SAML/OIDC SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC and delegated admin controls.

Key asks:
- Confirm supported protocols (SAML 2.0 / OIDC) and IdP metadata exchange.
- SCIM 2.0 capabilities: push/pull, PATCH support, group sync, bulk operations, error handling.
- Role/permission model and delegated admin workflows (can a user be admin in a tenant-scoped subset?).
- Audit logging retention and export options; ability to provide event-level logs for customers.
- Any tenant segmentation or multi-tenant isolation details relevant to regulated financial customers.

Please return your completed questionnaire and any sample mappings/configs by EOD Monday (2027-12-13). If you have templates or evidence (SAML metadata, SCIM mapping CSV, role matrix, SOC2), include them as attachments or links.

Thanks,
Alex Ruiz

Alex —

Appreciate the questionnaire. We've completed the form and attached a concise evidence package that addresses each of your bullets. Highlights up front:

- SSO: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. We provide SP metadata (redwood_idp_metadata.xml) and can ingest IdP metadata with automatic attribute mapping.
- SCIM: We implement SCIM 2.0 (RFC7643/7644) with PATCH, bulk create/update, group membership sync, and filtering. Our SCIM endpoint supports incremental change tokens and paged responses. Sample attribute mapping included (redwood_scim_mapping.csv).
- RBAC & Admin: We ship an account-level role matrix with hierarchical roles and delegated admin scopes. Admin roles can be tenant-scoped (e.g., "Tenant Admin" limited to a single tenant) or global ("Org Admin"). The admin role matrix and example policies are attached (redwood_admin_role_matrix.pdf).
- Audit & Logs: Event-level audit logs (authentication events, admin changes, SCIM syncs, API calls) are retained for 12 months by default; longer retention is available as an add-on. Logs can be exported via S3, pushed to customer SIEM via syslog/HTTPS webhook, or made available through a secure log-export job.
- Tenant isolation: For private/dedicated deployments we offer VPC-isolated control planes and optional customer-managed key encryption (KMS/HSM). Hosted customers get logical separation with strong access controls and per-tenant encryption keys.

We've also noted a few items where we'd like clarification from your security/identity team: SCIM change frequency expectations, expected SCIM error handling SLAs, and whether Mosaic prefers group-of-record or attribute-of-record for group membership.

I've copied Kimberly from our security engineering team — she'll add a short note on token/session controls and session termination rules below.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Identity & Integrations
Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side to make integration planning easier: 

- SCIM rate limits: our managed hosted endpoints allow bursts up to 300 requests/minute with steady-state 100 req/minute per tenant. For bulk onboarding we recommend the bulk endpoint (up to 10k records per job) which processes asynchronously and returns job status.
- Provisioning model: supports both just-in-time (JIT) provisioning via OIDC claims and SCIM push provisioning. Our SCIM implementation supports PATCH operations per RFC7644 and returns structured error responses for partial failures.
- Session/token controls: session lifetime is configurable at org level. Default OIDC access token lifetime is 1 hour; refresh token rotation is supported. Admin sessions can be forcibly terminated via the Admin API (session-revoke endpoint) and those events are logged in the audit stream.
- SCIM filtering & group sync: we support filter expressions for subgroup sync ("members[type eq \"User\"]"-style) and include group membership change deltas in webhook payloads.

If Mosaic prefers different rate limits for initial syncs, we can schedule a temporary elevated window or provide an import job.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference
